FT-002.adaptation: Accepted FT-002 rev 8: broader pinned corpus, repeated burst-edit and recovery performance gates, preserved source and capability identity, and byte/pixel parity published separately from compiler latency. Rev 7 just removed a parser quadratic that made a 500KB one-word edit 420ms; burst editing is the natural next risk because it is what real typing looks like and it is where reuse state could degrade across many consecutive edits rather than one. Note that open issue #21 remains unaddressed and is mine: a valid 500KB project emits 10.1MB in one reply and exceeds the 8 MiB runtime frame.

next_action: Awaiting rev 9 or the transport decision on issue #21. Remaining real gaps are greedy paragraph breaking, owned by FT-019, and hyphenation.
